original.finding: The frozen runner expected BAD_REQUEST/admission. The host rejected missing Direct with BAD_REQUEST/request. Its failed assertion triggered cleanup Stop, which returned HTTP500; the attempt failed and remains retained.

paired_observation.finding: The checked runner and fixed-UUID observation helper completed missing-Direct rejection, imported Direct, selected unavailable Scanlines, launched the exact linked Direct fallback on the same host process, and stopped to idle with a free lease.

phase_checked.finding: The phase-corrected runner accepted and retained BAD_REQUEST/request, then failed when the unscoped diagnostic health endpoint returned HTTP503. Cleanup Stop returned HTTP500. This attempt also remains failed.

classification: Operator-harness limitation and retained correction evidence; no production fix or new hardware action was performed to prepare this summary.

observation.explanation: The derived Go helper scopes diagnostic Health and Status through WithPairedTarget to the operator-fixed UUID, matching its existing lease observation scope. Normal launch/Stop routes and Python target/image/readiness, exact-status and lease checks are unchanged. Frozen sources/binary remain retained.

phase.explanation: Local composeVideoEntry reports the missing mandatory output. loadCoreLocked passes source-resolution errors to corePackageRequestFailure, which sets phase=request before dispatch. The derived runner changes only this phase expectation and saves the complete negative response before asserting.

scope: The passing partial run covers missing mandatory Direct and missing Scanlines falling back to linked Direct. It does not add corrupt-part or Scanlines-only physical coverage.
unresolved_limitation: The cause of the original unscoped Health HTTP503 and cleanup Stop HTTP500 is unresolved. The frozen helper hides the underlying observation error and discards unexpected response bodies. Paired-read success does not establish that the original failures were intentional, fixed, or generally harmless.
